title: Rapid 5xx spike after scheduler backoff + ephemeral proxy thundering during large embedding fanout
content:
description:
Issue summary: BrightWrite reports a sudden, sustained increase in 5xx responses (502/503) from their dedicated tenant beginning ~2026-03-13 09:22 UTC. The spike coincides with a large embedding upload + mixed small chat traffic. Impact: Customer-facing upload jobs failing, automated ingestion retries, and visible latency spikes for downstream queries. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod - us-east with reserved capacity. Steps to reproduce: 1) Upload a large embeddings batch (~120k vectors) via embeddings endpoint 2) Simultaneously send small chat requests to the same tenant 3) Observe API gateway 502/503 errors and runtime restarts/logged backoffs. Recent changes: no customer model pin changes; autoscaler applied a scheduler backoff tweak earlier today. Logs: see attached SRE logs and proxy traces referenced in investigation notes. 

investigation_notes:
Correlation: 09:22 UTC aligns with scheduler config sweep (auto-rollout) that changed backoff reset window for prewarm probes in us-east cluster.
api-gateway metrics: accept_queue_length increased 8x; 502s originate from upstream connection resets and proxy workers reporting 'watchdog: worker exited (signal 9)'.
"nvml logs" show transient GPU memory fragmentation and a sequence of quick model prefetches from embeddings shard coordinator which coincided with high ephemeral-proxy CPU. (see github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issue/987)
ephemeral-proxy behavior: high concurrency embedding uploads created many concurrent long-lived connections; scheduler backoff oscillation attempted rapid prewarm then backed off, resulting in connection pile-up and thundering-herd of ephemeral proxies trying to recover.
Heap/oom: Several runtime proxy workers exhibited OOM-like exit traces; container restarts caused upstream to drop connections, amplifying 502s at API gateway.
Hypothesis A: Scheduler backoff parameter change reduced the damping on prewarm probes, amplifying concurrent prefetches and causing ephemeral-proxy CPU/memory thrash leading to worker exits.
Hypothesis B: Embedding bulk upload pattern interacts poorly with streaming chat traffic (mix of long-lived and short-lived connections) causing accept-queue head-of-line blocking and upstream resets.
Short-term mitigations executed: tenant ingress rate cap applied; advised customer to reduce embedding upload concurrency; cleared prefetched KV cache entries for affected shard to reduce spike load.
Monitoring: set alerting on accept_queue growth (>200) and proxy worker exit rate (>5/min).

resolution_notes:
Workaround: Ingress rate cap and temporary concurrency limit on BrightWrite's tenant allowed embedding uploads to complete with <2% 5xx within 3 hours.
Fix deployed: Scheduler hotfix rolled back the aggressive backoff reset and added jitter to prewarm probe start times (deployed 2026-03-14 08:30 UTC).
Runtime changes: Runtime team updated ephemeral-proxy to better cap memory per-worker and added soft-limits to avoid hard OOM exits (deployed canary 2026-03-14 09:50 UTC).
Follow-ups: 1) Create a dedicated runbook for mixed-traffic (embedding + streaming) tenant patterns. 2) Increase accept_queue default sizing for dedicated pools and revisit autoscaler thresholds. 3) Add test that simulates large embedding upload + chat traffic for regression testing. Owner: Diego Morales / Runtime team. Deadline: 2026-03-21.
Customer communication: Support committed to a postmortem and permanent mitigations; customer acknowledged and requested timeline for runbook and autoscale improvements.
